packet.headline_seed: How Trump's White House ballroom plan has doubled in size and cost over a year
packet.description_seed: BBC Verify examines how the biggest change to the White House in decades has transformed in the last year.

what: How Trump's White House ballroom plan has doubled in size and cost over a year

clean_source_blocks.text: In the year since US President Donald Trump announced plans to build a new ballroom at the White House, the proposals have grown to include a rooftop "drone port", an underground hospital and "top secret" military facilities - and the estimated price has doubled to $400m (£300m). Despite promises from Trump that the project wouldn't cost US taxpayers any money, Republicans have requested additional funds from Congress for security around the complex - at a time when Americans are struggling with rising living costs linked to the Iran war. The president indicated from the outset that the new ballroom is needed to "accommodate people for grand parties, State Visits", and more recently said it is "vital for National Security". BBC Verify has examined how the biggest change to the White House in decades has transformed over the past year.
BBC Verify examines how the biggest change to the White House in decades has transformed in the last year.

President Donald Trump took to TruthSocial Wednesday morning to defend the expense of his highly touted White House ballroom amid reports that Congress plans to seek $1 billion in taxpayer dollars for the project. Trump acknowledged that the price tag for the ballroom project located in the now-demolished East Wing has doubled since he first proposed it last summer, but the president insisted that the ballooning costs are necessary due to the venue being much larger and more luxurious than initially planned. “The only reason the cost has changed is because, after deep rooted studies, it is approximately twice the size, and a far higher quality, than the original proposal, which would not have been adequate to handle the necessary events, meetings, and even future Inaugurations,” Trump wrote.

Trump’s early-morning missive notably did not include the staggering figure put forward by Congress but took a passing shot at the media, which he claims failed to report that the ballroom will be completed earlier than planned and for less money. “The original price was 200 Million Dollars, the double sized, highest quality completed project will be something less than 400 Million Dollars. It will be magnificent, safe, and secure!” he said. “This was a necessary change, it was done long ago, but the Fake News failed to report it, trying to make it look like there was a cost overrun. Actually, it is coming in ahead of schedule, and under budget!”

[Lähde: BBC World]
In the year since US President Donald Trump announced plans to build a new ballroom at the White House, the proposals have grown to include a rooftop "drone port", an underground hospital and "top secret" military facilities - and the estimated price has doubled to $400m (£300m).

Despite promises from Trump that the project wouldn't cost US taxpayers any money, Republicans have requested additional funds from Congress for security around the complex - at a time when Americans are struggling with rising living costs linked to the Iran war.

The president indicated from the outset that the new ballroom is needed to "accommodate people for grand parties, State Visits", and more recently said it is "vital for National Security".

BBC Verify has examined how the biggest change to the White House in decades has transformed over the past year.

On 6 June last year, Trump announced on his social media platform Truth Social that he had inspected the site where a new ballroom would be built, promising it would "go up quickly" and would be "very much in keeping with the magnificent White House itself".

"These are the 'fun' projects I do while thinking about the World Economy, the United States, China, Russia, and lots of other Countries, places, and events," he added.

The following month his administration revealed plans for a new "White House State Ballroom" to be built where the "small, heavily changed, and reconstructed East Wing currently sits", adding that its "theme and architectural heritage will be almost identical" to the historic main building.

The statement said the ballroom promised to be a "much-needed and exquisite addition of approximately 90,000 total square feet of ornately designed and carefully crafted space". It added that the structure would be able to seat 650 people, a "significant increase" on the 200-seated capacity of the East Room in the main residence.

The East Room is the primary space in the White House for official ceremonies and events and was used to host King Charles' state banquet in April. But larger events in recent years, such as French President Emmanuel Macron's state dinner in 2022 that had more than 300 guests, have been hosted in temporary tent structures built on the White House's south lawn.

The administration said the ballroom's construction would start later that year and be completed "long before" the end of Trump's second term in January 2029.

President Donald Trump took to TruthSocial Wednesday morning to defend the expense of his highly touted White House ballroom amid reports that Congress plans to seek $1 billion in taxpayer dollars for the project.

Trump acknowledged that the price tag for the ballroom project located in the now-demolished East Wing has doubled since he first proposed it last summer, but the president insisted that the ballooning costs are necessary due to the venue being much larger and more luxurious than initially planned.

“The only reason the cost has changed is because, after deep rooted studies, it is approximately twice the size, and a far higher quality, than the original proposal, which would not have been adequate to handle the necessary events, meetings, and even future Inaugurations,” Trump wrote.

The president appeared to be responding to news that congressional Republicans are seeking $1 billion for the project as part of an upcoming $70 billion reconciliation bill that will fund Immigration and Customs Enforcement as well as the U.S. Border Patrol through 2029. The text of the funding legislation allocates $1 billion to the Secret Service for “the purposes of security adjustments and upgrades including within the perimeter fence of the White House Compound to support enhancements by the United States Secret Service relating to the East Wing Modernization Project, including above-ground and below-ground security features.” Trump has also indicated that prominent private donors were expected to help fund the project, including Amazon, Google, and Palantir.

Trump’s early-morning missive notably did not include the staggering figure put forward by Congress but took a passing shot at the media, which he claims failed to report that the ballroom will be completed earlier than planned and for less money.

“The original price was 200 Million Dollars, the double sized, highest quality completed project will be something less than 400 Million Dollars. It will be magnificent, safe, and secure!” he said. “This was a necessary change, it was done long ago, but the Fake News failed to report it, trying to make it look like there was a cost overrun. Actually, it is coming in ahead of schedule, and under budget!”

payload.title: Trump puolustaa Valkoisen talon juhlasalin kasvaneita kustannuksia
payload.summary: Donald Trumpin suunnitelma uudesta juhlasalista Valkoiseen taloon on kasvanut vuoden aikana huomattavasti: arvioitu hinta on noussut noin 400 miljoonaan dollariin ja hankkeen sisältö on laajentunut turvallisuuteen liittyvillä osilla.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trumpin suunnitelma rakentaa Valkoiseen taloon uusi juhlasali on kasvanut vuoden aikana sekä kooltaan että hinnaltaan. Hankkeen arvioitu kustannus on noussut noin 400 miljoonaan dollariin eli noin 300 miljoonaan puntaan, kun alkuperäinen hintalappu oli Trumpin mukaan 200 miljoonaa dollaria.

## Suunnitelma on laajentunut

Valkoisen talon muutosta on kuvattu yhdeksi rakennuksen suurimmista vuosikymmeniin. Alun perin juhlasalia perusteltiin tarpeella järjestää suuria juhlia, valtiovierailuja ja muita edustustilaisuuksia. Sittemmin suunnitelmiin on liitetty myös kattotasolle sijoittuva droonien käyttöön tarkoitettu alue, maanalainen sairaala sekä salaisiksi kuvattuja sotilaallisia tiloja.

Trump on viime aikoina perustellut hanketta myös kansallisen turvallisuuden näkökulmasta. Hänen mukaansa laajennettu ja laadukkaampi kokonaisuus on välttämätön, koska alkuperäinen suunnitelma ei olisi riittänyt tarvittaviin tapahtumiin, kokouksiin ja tuleviin virkaanastujaisiin.

## Kustannuksista kiistellään

Trump on aiemmin luvannut, ettei hanke maksaisi yhdysvaltalaisille veronmaksajille. Samalla republikaanit ovat kuitenkin pyytäneet kongressilta lisärahoitusta Valkoisen talon alueen turvallisuusjärjestelyihin. Keskustelu kustannuksista käydään tilanteessa, jossa monien amerikkalaisten arkea painavat Iranin sotaan liitetyt elinkustannusten nousut.

Raporttien mukaan kongressissa on ollut esillä jopa miljardin dollarin veronmaksajarahoitus hankkeeseen liittyviin kuluihin. Trump ei omassa viestissään käsitellyt tätä lukua, vaan arvosteli mediaa ja väitti hankkeen valmistuvan etuajassa ja alle budjetin.

## Trump puolustaa muutosta

Trump puolusti hankkeen hintaa Truth Social -palvelussa keskiviikkoaamuna. Hän myönsi hinnan kaksinkertaistuneen, mutta sanoi syyn olevan se, että hanke on tarkempien selvitysten jälkeen noin kaksi kertaa alkuperäistä suurempi ja laadultaan korkeampi.

Trumpin mukaan valmis kokonaisuus maksaa alle 400 miljoonaa dollaria. Hän kuvasi muutosta tarpeelliseksi ja sanoi, että aiempi ehdotus ei olisi ollut riittävä Valkoisen talon tuleviin tarpeisiin.
summary_bullets: Valkoisen talon uuden juhlasalin arvioitu hinta on noussut noin 400 miljoonaan dollariin.
Suunnitelmiin on liitetty juhlasalin lisäksi turvallisuuteen ja kriisivalmiuteen liittyviä tiloja.
Trump sanoo hankkeen kasvaneen, koska alkuperäinen suunnitelma ei olisi riittänyt tarvittaviin tapahtumiin.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketissa annettuihin tietoihin. Kongressin mahdollinen miljardin dollarin rahoitus mainitaan raportoituna esillä olleena lukuna, ei vahvistettuna lopullisena kustannuksena.
